definitions.explanation: An informal, somewhat old-fashioned way to refer to one's husband. Often carries a traditional connotation of the husband as head of the household.
The master or proprietor of an establishment such as an inn or a tea ceremony host. Also used for the host of a tea gathering.

examples.japanese: うちの{亭主|ていしゅ}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My husband is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {亭主|ていしゅ}{関白|かんぱく}な{男性|だんせい}は{今|いま}の{時代|じだい}には{合|あ}わない。
examples.english: A domineering husband doesn't fit the current era.

examples.japanese: {亭主|ていしゅ}が{丁寧|ていねい}にお{茶|ちゃ}を{点|た}てた。
examples.english: The host carefully prepared the tea.

examples.japanese: {旅館|りょかん}の{亭主|ていしゅ}が{笑顔|えがお}で{迎|むか}えてくれた。
examples.english: The proprietor of the inn welcomed us with a smile.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{亭主|ていしゅ}は{三代目|さんだいめ}だそうだ。
examples.english: I hear the owner of this shop is the third generation.

notes:
USAGE:
As "husband," {亭主|ていしゅ} sounds somewhat old-fashioned and informal. It is typically used by wives referring to their own husbands in casual speech. Younger speakers tend to prefer {夫|おっと} or {旦那|だんな}.

The compound {亭主|ていしゅ}{関白|かんぱく} (lit. "husband regent") describes a domineering husband who expects to be waited on.

As "master/host," {亭主|ていしゅ} is used in tea ceremony ({茶道|さどう}) to refer to the person hosting and serving tea.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {亭主|ていしゅ}{関白|かんぱく}: domineering husband
- うちの{亭主|ていしゅ}: my husband (casual)
- {旅館|りょかん}の{亭主|ていしゅ}: innkeeper
- お{茶|ちゃ}の{亭主|ていしゅ}: tea ceremony host
